chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Humran, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about pelting the Jamarat, so he said: 'They used to all be pelted on the Day of Nahr (sacrifice). So I used to pelt them all after that.' Then I narrated it to him, so he said to me: 'Are you not pleased that you should do as Ali (peace be upon him) used to do?' So I left it.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir, peace be upon him)
key_terms.رَمْيِ الْجِمَارِ: Pelting the Jamarat (ritual throwing of pebbles)
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct method for pelting the Jamarat according to the practice of Imam Ali (peace be upon him)?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the jurisprudential evolution of pelting the Jamarat, contrasting the Prophet’s practice of pelting all stones on the Day of Nahr with the established Sunnah of Imam Ali (peace be upon him). It underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on emulating the Ahl al-Bayt’s specific ritual practices as the definitive model for Hajj rites.
